basis: Fibromatosis arises in plantar fascia; nodules reflect fascial lesions. Paresthesia alone is not nerve damage; peripheral neuropathy occurs in <30%.
Immune-mediated epidermal necrosis; destructive oral mucositis occurs in >80% and ocular epithelial injury in roughly 50–80%, beyond transient conjunctival injection.
Hereditary optic nerve degeneration; optic pallor, visual field constriction and reduced acuity occur in 2/2 reported patients.
Persistent inherited neutrophil proliferation with splenomegaly; blood, marrow and spleen fall within the same axis. No established immunodeficiency.
Umbrella for spirochaetal bacterial infections; organ targets vary across Borrelia, Treponema and Leptospira infections.
Defining diaphyseal bone sclerosis and marrow dysfunction with anemia/cytopenias. Nonspecific immune-system annotations do not establish immunodeficiency.
Developmental impairment, skeletal/digital defects and structural ocular anomalies characterize the syndrome; cardiac and urinary malformations occur in <30%.
Congenital smooth muscle hamartoma is a dermal lesion, often with hypertrichosis. Dermal smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle; hemihypertrophy alone is not damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal/digital abnormalities characterize the syndrome; variable ocular anomalies lack evidence of occurrence in ≥30%.
KRT13-related white sponge nevus is a keratinization disorder principally affecting oral mucosa; the skin-disorder ancestry does not establish cutaneous disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal defects define the syndrome; strabismus affects 4/7 (~57%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Clonal marrow mast-cell proliferation; persistent cutaneous infiltration occurs in 80–99% and bone loss in 30–79%. Abdominal cramps alone do not establish gut damage.
Hereditary prostate malignancy originates in a reproductive organ outside the axes; prostate is not an endocrine gland.
Most mixed germ cell tumors arise in testis or ovary, outside the axes. CNS and mediastinal origins are site-specific minority subtypes, not generalizable to this umbrella.
Progressive upper motor neuron degeneration defines disease. Weakness and dysphagia are neurologic manifestations; skeletal muscle atrophy is reported in <30%.
Degeneration and atrophy directly affect the thyroid endocrine gland; an autoimmune cause is not specified.
The defining abnormalities are biliary tract malformation and renal tubular dysfunction; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Airway ciliary dysfunction causes chronic respiratory disease; middle-ear clearance dysfunction with recurrent otitis occurs in 2/5 (40%). Situs inversus alone is not damage.
POGLUT1-related reticulate pigmentation and epidermal abnormalities define this cutaneous disease; the glycosylation ancestor does not clearly establish a metabolic phenotype.
Clonal myeloid blasts occupy marrow and blood. Extramedullary involvement is uncommon; recurrent infections reflect hematopoietic failure, not an infectious mechanism.
Skeletal malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment define FS2. Definition explicitly excludes GI atresia, conflicting with HPO entries; GI involvement is therefore withheld.
Spondylometaphyseal bone dysplasia defines disease. Hypertension, cardiomegaly and developmental delay are reported, but their frequencies are unestablished.
Inherited tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis defect causes central neurotransmitter deficiency and neurodevelopmental/movement impairment; oculogyric crises are neurologic.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric condition without a qualifying organ axis; no direct common organ damage is inherent in this diagnosis.
Rickettsiaceae infection characteristically targets vascular endothelium, causing small-vessel vasculitis. Transient rash does not establish additional skin damage.
